# Incident Report: 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.17.0.99 | Consistent source IP across all suspicious flows |
| MAC | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 | ARP reply and Ethernet source for 172.17.0.99 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT | DHCP Option 12 hostname (frames 1, 3); confirmed by NBNS registration `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>/<20>` |
| Windows domain | bepositive.com (AD domain, DC = WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19 at 172.17.0.17) | DNS SRV lookups for `_ldap._tcp...bepositive.com`, NBNS name `WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19` |
| Logged-in user | afletcher | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic from 172.17.0.99 to the DC |
| Extra host alias | BEPOSITIVE (NBNS `BEPOSITIVE<00>/<1e>`) — appears to be a secondary NetBIOS name on the same host, not a separate device (same IP/MAC) | NBNS name-registration frames |

Note: the ET/GPL "SMB NTLMSSP overflow / IPC$ / kerberos overflow" alerts (17:33-17:34 UTC) between 172.17.0.99 and the domain controller 172.17.0.17 are standard AD authentication protocol traffic (SMB session setup, kerberos ticketing) that trips generic exploit-signature rules on protocol fields; nothing in the packets indicates actual exploitation. Classified as benign/false-positive AD traffic.

## Malware Family
**Koi Stealer** (also tracked with an associated loader/gate component). Attribution: **signature-confirmed** — Suricata rule `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` fired 48 times (event #3.1504) against the exact `POST /foots.php` traffic pattern captured and independently verified below via `tshark follow,tcp`.

Infection timeline (UTC):
- 17:32:31 — capture start, host boot/DHCP, normal LAN/AD traffic.
- 17:35:04 — TLS session to 46.254.34.201:443, SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (compromised/malvertising site, likely the initial delivery vector; content is TLS-encrypted so cannot be inspected further; flagged as suspicious but not confirmed malicious in-capture).
- 17:35:07 onward — repeated cleartext HTTP `POST /foots.php` beacons to 79.124.78.197:80 with a fixed bot GUID (`30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`), Internet Explorer-spoofed User-Agent, and short binary/base64-like payloads — classic stealer check-in/exfil beacon (matches ET alert, Event #3.1497 "GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser" and #3.1504).
- 17:35:11 — `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` and `POST /index.php` to the same IP, returning an encrypted/obfuscated blob (`HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`) — a PPI/loader "gate" checkout pattern (affiliate `subid`), consistent with a loader delivering the stealer.
- Beaconing to 79.124.78.197 continues at short intervals for the remainder of the capture (~96 `/foots.php` POSTs total).

No executable/PE payload body was recoverable from the capture (`tshark --export-objects http` yields only empty or non-executable response bodies for the C2 traffic), so no malware binary file name or SHA256 could be grounded in this evidence.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints**
- `79.124.78.197:80` — Koi Stealer HTTP CnC (POST /foots.php beacon + /index.php gate). Evidence: `tshark -Y http.request` list, TCP stream follow of frames 1668/2227, ET alert Event#3.1497/#3.1504.

**Suspicious/pre-C2 endpoint (unconfirmed)**
- `46.254.34.201:443` — TLS session, SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`, ~700KB transferred, immediately precedes the first Koi Stealer beacon. Likely delivery-chain hop; content not decryptable from capture, so listed as suspicious context rather than a confirmed IOC.

**Domains**
- None resolved for the C2 IP 79.124.78.197 — the malware connects directly to a bare IP (no DNS lookup precedes the HTTP traffic to it), itself a C2 tell.
- `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` — SNI of the suspicious pre-beacon TLS session to 46.254.34.201 (see above; unconfirmed role).

**URLs**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` (stealer check-in/exfil endpoint, ~96 requests)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` (loader gate lookup)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` (loader gate POST, returns encrypted blob)

**File names / hashes**
- None. No executable payload body was present in the exported HTTP objects from this capture; only the stealer's small POST bodies and empty/ack HTTP responses were recoverable. No SHA256 can be grounded in evidence.

## Benign Context (excluded from IOCs)
- `www.msftconnecttest.com`, `dns.msftncsi.com` — Windows NCSI connectivity checks.
- `acroipm2.adobe.com` (resolves legitimately to Akamai 23.220.251.47/.48) — Adobe ARM update-manager check, `GET /assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt`.
- `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`, `x1.c.lencr.org` — Windows CTL/CRL and Let's Encrypt OCSP/cert-transparency traffic.
- Microsoft/Office/MSN/Bing telemetry and content domains (`api.msn.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `officeclient.microsoft.com`, `settings-win.data.microsoft.com`, etc.).
- AD/domain traffic to 172.17.0.17 (DC WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19): DNS, LDAP/CLDAP, Kerberos, SMB/NBNS — normal domain-joined workstation behavior; the ET/GPL SMB/Kerberos "overflow" alerts against this traffic are signature false positives on protocol fields, not evidence of exploitation.

## Summary
Windows workstation DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user `afletcher` on the `bepositive.com` AD domain, was infected with **Koi Stealer** at approximately 17:35 UTC on 2024-09-04. Shortly after a TLS connection to a suspicious external site (SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`, 46.254.34.201), the host began sustained cleartext HTTP beaconing to C2 `79.124.78.197:80` (`/foots.php` check-ins carrying bot GUID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`, plus an `/index.php` loader/PPI gate with affiliate ID `qIOuKk7U`), confirmed by the ETPRO Koi Stealer signature and continuing for the remainder of the capture. No malware binary was recoverable from the traffic itself.
